source.question: e-9551
source.value:
First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as 

$$
\displaystyle{\oint\limits_{C}\mathbf{F}\cdot\mathrm{d}\mathbf{r}}
=
\oint\limits_{C} (y^2+\sin x) \: \mathrm{d}x + (3xy-\cos y) \: \mathrm{d}y.
$$

Green's theorem states that

$$
\oint\limits_{C} P\,\mathrm{d}x + Q\,\mathrm{d}y 
= \iint\limits_D \left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)\,\textrm d A.
$$

In our case, the region $D$ and its boundary $C$ satisfy the conditions of Green's theorem:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14061894/assets/798665574b8f0e11d991bb0d934efd01bdeb65840c2e86498be4edbc59578439.png)

Since $P(x,y)= y^2+\sin x$ and $Q(x,y)= 3xy-\cos y,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=3y.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({y}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,dx+(xy-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3y-2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the region $D$ can be represented in polar coordinates as

$$
\Delta = \big\{ (r,\theta) \: : \: 0\leq r \leq 2,\: 0 \leq \theta \leq 2\pi  \big\}.
$$

The change of variables formula for plane polar coordinates states that

$$
\iint\limits_{D} f(x,y) \ \mathrm d A = \iint\limits_{\Delta} \ f(r \cos\theta, r\sin\theta) \:  r \ \mathrm d r \mathrm d \theta.
$$

Therefore, we can write our double integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,{\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $r^2\sin\theta.$

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as 

$$
\displaystyle{\oint\limits_{C}\mathbf{F}\cdot\mathrm{d}\mathbf{r}}
=
\oint\limits_{C} (2y + \ln{(\sqrt{x+5})}) \: \mathrm{d}x + \left( e^{y/3} + 3x \right) \: \mathrm{d}y.
$$

Green's theorem states that

$$
\oint\limits_{C} P\,\mathrm{d}x + Q\,\mathrm{d}y 
= \iint\limits_D \left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)\,\textrm d A.
$$

In our case, the region $D$ and its boundary $C$ satisfy the conditions of Green's theorem:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14061894/assets/e4c7913793a4b08916a832e575c5b2c167d5dfeec244eea23857731df1e514e7.png)

Since $P(x,y)= 2y + \ln{(\sqrt{x+5})}$ and $Q(x,y)=e^{y/3} + 3x,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(2y+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x+5}))\,dx+({e}^{y/3}+3x)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3-2)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the region $D$ can be represented in polar coordinates as

$$
\Delta = \left\{ (r,\theta) \: : \: 0 \leq r \leq 3, \: \dfrac{\pi}{2} \leq \theta \leq 2\pi \right\}.
$$

The change of variables formula for plane polar coordinates states that

$$
\iint\limits_{D} f(x,y) \ \mathrm d A = \iint\limits_{\Delta} \ f(r \cos\theta, r\sin\theta) \:  r \ \mathrm d r \mathrm d \theta.
$$

Therefore, we can write our double integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }\,{\int }_{0}^{3}r\,dr\,d\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
